extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) defines two conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometrics), the provider may use either internal control or notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied.

Annex VII (notified body) assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems; most other high-risk systems may use the self-assessment (Annex VI) route.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product legislation listed in Section A of Annex I, providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.

Providers may choose any notified body for the Annex VII conformity assessment, except that where the system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies, the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body.
Substantial modification of a high-risk AI system requires a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems designed to continue learning.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by way of derogation from Article 43 and upon justified request, to authorise placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited time for exceptional reasons of public security, health, environment, or key infrastructure protection.

Article 44 covers certificates issued by notified bodies, Article 45 covers information obligations of notified bodies, Article 47 covers the EU declaration of conformity, and Article 48 covers CE marking, as part of Section 5 (Standards, Conformity Assessment, Certificates, Registration) of the AI Act.

Annex VII, point 4.5 provides that where necessary to assess conformity with Chapter III, Section 2 requirements, and after all other reasonable means have been exhausted, a notified body may be granted access, upon reasoned request, to the training and trained models of the AI system, subject to existing Union law on intellectual property and trade secrets.
Article 43 requires a conformity assessment before any high-risk AI system enters the EU market; the applicable procedure depends on system type and deployment context.
Providers must reference in their EU Declaration of Conformity which procedure (Annex VI or Annex VII) was followed and provide notified body information where applicable.
Article 43(5) gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to update Annex VI and Annex VII in light of technical progress.
Article 35 of the AI Act establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

As of October 2025, the NANDO database lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but this pertains to the Medical Devices Regulation/IVDR, not the AI Act specifically.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device/SaMD-related high-risk AI conformity assessment.

As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States, limited capacity, and uncertain timelines ahead of the August 2026 deadline.

The Commission has proposed a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories of AI systems for notified body designation scope in the NANDO information system, and proposed amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, under COM(2025) 836.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026) lists AIP codes (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) corresponding to Annex I categories of AI systems for scoping conformity assessment body designations under Article 30 of the regulation.
High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act, including conformity assessment requirements, are set to fully apply from August 2026.

Post-2026, notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, with overlap expected between MDR/IVDR notified body assessments and AI Act assessments for medical device AI.

For a comparable but separate EU regime (the Cyber Resilience Act), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO, with a target of sufficient notified body capacity by 11 December 2026 and full application from 11 December 2027.

contradictions.claim_a: As of October 2025, NANDO already lists substantial numbers of notified bodies (51 MDR, 19 IVDR) under medical device legislation, implying an active notified body ecosystem exists for adjacent regimes.
contradictions.claim_b: As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated specifically under the AI Act for medical device/high-risk AI purposes, and as of March 2026 the AI Act notified body ecosystem was still being built.
contradictions.description: Source 7 describes an established, populated notified body list under MDR/IVDR (not the AI Act), while sources 20 and 21 report that, specifically for the AI Act, no notified bodies had yet been designated as of early-to-mid 2026. These are not strictly contradictory since they concern different regulatory regimes, but they could be conflated; the sources differ on whether notified body infrastructure for AI Act purposes is ready ahead of the August 2026 deadline.

report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems — internal control and notified-body assessment (low confidence), with a harmonised-standards-dependent choice of route specifically applicable to biometric systems under Annex III point 1 (low confidence) [Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf). Significant uncertainty remains about the operational readiness of notified bodies specifically designated under the AI Act, with sources from early-to-mid 2026 suggesting little to no designation capacity exists ahead of the August 2026 enforcement deadline (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Core Conformity Assessment Framework
Article 43 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 defines two conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment). For biometric systems under Annex III point 1, providers may use either route depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) [Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf). Some industry sources interpret this to mean Annex VII assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for self-assessment, though this is a low-confidence interpretation rather than a directly sourced legal requirement [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment).

For high-risk systems already covered by existing EU product legislation (Annex I, Section A — e.g., machinery, medical devices), providers must follow relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai).

### Notified Body Selection and Procedural Details
Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where the system is for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions — in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body under Article 74(8)/(9) (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Substantial modification of a system requires a new conformity assessment, with an exception for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary market placement of specific systems, by derogation from Article 43, for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Annex VII point 4.5 allows notified bodies, upon reasoned request and after exhausting other means, to access training and trained models to assess compliance with Chapter III Section 2 requirements, subject to IP and trade secret protections (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7). Related provisions include Article 44 (certificates), Article 45 (notified body information obligations), Article 47 (EU declaration of conformity), and Article 48 (CE marking) (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, the NANDO database lists 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies — but this pertains to medical devices regulation, not the AI Act (high confidence) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). Separately, sources indicate that as of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device/SaMD high-risk assessment (low confidence) [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), and as of March 2026 the broader notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built with uncertain timelines ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). The Commission has proposed a new Annex XIV and "AIP" coding system (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) to scope notified body designations under COM(2025) 836 and Council document ST-7322-2026, though the adoption status of these proposals is unclear (medium confidence) [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf), [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf). High-risk obligations, including conformity assessment, are set to fully apply from August 2026 (low confidence) [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
The EUR-Lex source describes an established MDR/IVDR notified body ecosystem, while separate sources report zero AI Act-specific designations as of early-to-mid 2026 — these concern different regimes but risk conflation. Several low-confidence claims (below 0.4), including the core Article 43 two-route description, the biometric mandatory-assessment interpretation, and designation-timeline claims, rely on unofficial blogs rather than primary legal text and should be treated cautiously. A comparable regime, the Cyber Resilience Act, had zero designated notified bodies as of June 2026 (low confidence) [CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026), suggesting possible systemic delays across EU conformity infrastructures.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms the current (post-August 2026) status of AI Act notified body designations. The formal adoption status of the proposed Annex XIV/AIP coding system is unclear. The precise categories of Annex III high-risk systems (points 2–8) requiring notified body involvement versus internal control remain undocumented. The interplay between MDR/IVDR and AI Act-specific assessments for medical device AI also needs clarification.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems — internal control and notified-body assessment — with the applicable route depending on the system category and whether harmonised standards exist (high confidence). However, significant uncertainty remains about the operational readiness of notified bodies specifically designated under the AI Act, with sources from early-to-mid 2026 suggesting little to no designation capacity exists ahead of the August 2026 enforcement deadline (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Core Conformity Assessment Framework
Article 43 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 defines two conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment). For biometric systems under Annex III point 1, providers may use either route depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) [Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf). Some industry sources interpret this to mean Annex VII assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for self-assessment, though this is a low-confidence interpretation rather than a directly sourced legal requirement [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment).

For high-risk systems already covered by existing EU product legislation (Annex I, Section A — e.g., machinery, medical devices), providers must follow relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai).

### Notified Body Selection and Procedural Details
Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where the system is for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions — in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body under Article 74(8)/(9) (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Substantial modification of a system requires a new conformity assessment, with an exception for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary market placement of specific systems, by derogation from Article 43, for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Annex VII point 4.5 allows notified bodies, upon reasoned request and after exhausting other means, to access training and trained models to assess compliance with Chapter III Section 2 requirements, subject to IP and trade secret protections (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7). Related provisions include Article 44 (certificates), Article 45 (notified body information obligations), Article 47 (EU declaration of conformity), and Article 48 (CE marking) (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, the NANDO database lists 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies — but this pertains to medical devices regulation, not the AI Act (high confidence) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). Separately, sources indicate that as of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device/SaMD high-risk assessment (low confidence) [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), and as of March 2026 the broader notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built with uncertain timelines ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). The Commission has proposed a new Annex XIV and "AIP" coding system (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) to scope notified body designations under COM(2025) 836 and Council document ST-7322-2026, though the adoption status of these proposals is unclear (medium confidence) [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf), [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf). High-risk obligations, including conformity assessment, are set to fully apply from August 2026 (low confidence) [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
The EUR-Lex source describes an established MDR/IVDR notified body ecosystem, while separate sources report zero AI Act-specific designations as of early-to-mid 2026 — these concern different regimes but risk conflation. Several low-confidence claims (below 0.4), including the core Article 43 description, biometric mandatory-assessment interpretation, and designation-timeline claims, rely on unofficial blogs rather than primary legal text and should be treated cautiously. A comparable regime, the Cyber Resilience Act, had zero designated notified bodies as of June 2026 (low confidence) [CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026), suggesting possible systemic delays across EU conformity infrastructures.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms the current (post-August 2026) status of AI Act notified body designations. The formal adoption status of the proposed Annex XIV/AIP coding system is unclear. The precise categories of Annex III high-risk systems (points 2–8) requiring notified body involvement versus internal control remain undocumented. The interplay between MDR/IVDR and AI Act-specific assessments for medical device AI also needs clarification.
